niche.habitat: Lateral junctions of basalt/salt Lanes; buried in crust.

body: Flattened, salt-crusted exoskeleton with six broad tarsi and elastic forelimbs.

chains.trait: Exoskeleton plates mirror salt crystallization patterns.
links: Plates mimic salt -> Hides against bright road surface -> Predator needs cryptic ambush position -> Road is the primary hunting ground.
Bright road -> High contrast environment -> Visual predators require visual camouflage -> F1 star spectrum and F14 salt flats create blinding white roads.

skill.effect: The creature burrows into a salt crust, becoming nearly invisible and hard to spot for a short while.

chains.weakness: Rain or wet wind dissolves salt crust, revealing the predator.
observe: Exoskeleton flakes match surrounding salt geometry.
Plates shift microscopically to match local crystallization.
Predator remains motionless until vibration threshold is met.

journal.en: It does not walk; it becomes the road.

plausibility.summary: Match the statistics of the crust: matte, broadband-white, grain-sized roughness at the scale prey can resolve, with only the dorsum exposed by burial. Replace instant crystal-shifting with moult- or chromatophore-based change over days. Keep the wet-wind weakness (F10/F15): a wetted crust changes brightness and clumps, betraying the outline. Explain six legs as one lost arachnid pair, and drop the numeric move values.
fixes: Match the statistics of the crust: matte, broadband-white, grain-sized roughness at the scale prey can resolve, with only the dorsum exposed by burial. Replace instant crystal-shifting with moult- or chromatophore-based change over days. Keep the wet-wind weakness (F10/F15): a wetted crust changes brightness and clumps, betraying the outline. Explain six legs as one lost arachnid pair, and drop the numeric move values.

analogues.organism: Crab spiders (Misumena/Thomisus) switch white-yellow over days; shore crabs tune chromatophores to substrate in minutes; antlion larvae and sand-burying vipers vanish into their substrate; peppered moth melanism shows the selection.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Fluid-filled sensory pits detect low-frequency vibrations.
links: Pits detect vibration -> Locates rolling prey before sight -> Prey moves too fast for visual reaction -> F18 roller speed exceeds legged pursuit.
Vibration detection -> Efficient targeting on featureless ground -> F9 sound/vibration travels well in 1.5-bar air and hard ground.

skill.effect: The creature senses approaching prey through the ground, revealing their movement trails even when vision is obscured.

chains.weakness: Wind noise (F10 gusts) masks vibration cues, blinding the predator.
observe: Sensory pits twitch in response to distant wheels.
Predator tracks vibration source with fluid-shifts.
Predator attacks only when vibration frequency matches rolling signature.

plausibility.summary: Couple the pits to the tarsi and ground rather than the air: gusts (F10) then mask cues by shaking loose salt and by the hunter's own movement, which keeps the stated weakness honest. Retain tread-cadence recognition, the best physical detail in this chain; state the range as approximate and remove numeric move values.
fixes: Couple the pits to the tarsi and ground rather than the air: gusts (F10) then mask cues by shaking loose salt and by the hunter's own movement, which keeps the stated weakness honest. Retain tread-cadence recognition, the best physical detail in this chain; state the range as approximate and remove numeric move values.

analogues.organism: Spiders' slit sensilla and subgenual organs detect substrate-borne vibration; stink bugs and treehoppers communicate through substrata; the fish lateral line is the aquatic analogue, sensing particle motion rather than air pressure.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Magnetite deposits in strike limb disrupt prey navigation.
links: Magnetite disrupts navigation -> Prey swerves or stops -> Easier capture -> F24 prey uses magnetite to follow Lanes.
Magnetite deposit -> Local magnetic anomaly -> F7 crustal remanence provides magnetic 'map' for navigation.

skill.effect: The creature strikes with a magnetite limb, strongly disorienting nearby prey and forcing them to halt for a short while.

chains.weakness: Strong external magnetic fields (e.g., player magnetism) can confuse El Cruce's own strike timing.
observe: Prey swerves erratically as El Cruce prepares to strike.
Magnetite glint in the limb catches the K3V light.
Prey stops or spins, losing momentum.

journal.en: It steals the road from beneath their wheels.

plausibility.summary: Scale the effect to strike distance (roughly 1-2 m), require a visible magnetite mass in the limb, and replace the forced stop with a skid and heading error; the hunter desensitising its own compass mid-strike is a good, honest cost. Treat 'prey stops and spins' as exaggeration. Keep the magnetic-decoy secret: a detached nodule neatly exploits F24.
fixes: Scale the effect to strike distance (roughly 1-2 m), require a visible magnetite mass in the limb, and replace the forced stop with a skid and heading error; the hunter desensitising its own compass mid-strike is a good, honest cost. Treat 'prey stops and spins' as exaggeration. Keep the magnetic-decoy secret: a detached nodule neatly exploits F24.

analogues.organism: Magnetotactic bacteria orient to fields; animal magnetoreception; electric fish jamming avoidance is the signal-jamming analogue; magnetic-pulse disruption of pigeon homing, from memory, unverified.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Broad, flat tarsi for walking on loose crust.
links: Broad tarsi -> Prevents sinking in dunes/crust -> Off-road mobility -> F22 off-road refuges are essential for survival.
Off-road mobility -> Lanes are islands in rough terrain -> F13 low relief but broken crust surrounds Lanes.

skill.effect: El Cruce traverses loose terrain without stamina loss, allowing flank attacks.

chains.weakness: Slow on hard Lanes; relies on ambush rather than pursuit.
observe: Tarsi spread wide to distribute weight.
Predator moves silently on dune fields.
El Cruce retreats off-road when not hunting.

journal.en: The road is its throne; the dunes are its home.

plausibility.summary: Attribute Lane slowness to ambush posture, heat and ground clearance rather than foot width; specify claw-or-grit grip at the ice edge for glissen, or drop the ice claim. Use F27 hollow crust as a weakness: even a broad-footed hunter can be let down by a sumper's 2 m sinkhole.
fixes: Attribute Lane slowness to ambush posture, heat and ground clearance rather than foot width; specify claw-or-grit grip at the ice edge for glissen, or drop the ice claim. Use F27 hollow crust as a weakness: even a broad-footed hunter can be let down by a sumper's 2 m sinkhole.

analogues.organism: Solifugid camel spiders and dune beetles use widened or hairy tarsi as sand shoes; camels and snowshoe hares are the load-spreading scaling analogue; fringe-toed lizards on sand.

body_plan.origin: Six-legged arachnoid lineage adapted for flat-surface locomotion.

secrets: The magnetite limb can be harvested to create a magnetic decoy that lures Skirls off-course.
El Cruce can 'taste' the salt composition to distinguish Karrow from Tucket before striking.
moments: A straight, white road. No wind. A single ripple in the salt crust, and then the road is gone.

journal.en: It waits where the roads kiss.
